summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked). All empirical items are PENDING. Q1 is designed as a two-definition comparison: the administrative urban share from Census 2021 by local-level type (post-2017 restructuring, which classifies extensive rural areas as municipal) versus a functional grid-based share from GHSL Degree of Urbanisation (with WorldPop cross-check), plus the UN WUP/WDI series with the 2017 definitional break flagged. Q2 builds a service-gap table (piped water, sanitation, solid waste; scheme functionality) by municipality type from Census 2021 household tables, NDHS 2022, JMP and NWASH, keeping census counts, survey estimates and JMP modelled ladders separate. Q3 measures 2011-2021 secondary-city growth on harmonised boundaries (2011 VDC to 2017 local-level concordance) and flags hazard exposure with 13A. Solid-waste coverage lacks any located municipal-level source. 21 source leads (11 reused from the shared register or catalog, 10 new general-knowledge URLs flagged unverified).

findings.claim: Q1: Urban population share under the current (post-2017) administrative classification: population of metropolitan, sub-metropolitan and municipalities as share of total, Census 2021.
findings.note: Census 2021 by local-level type. Administrative definition since 2017 restructuring classifies large rural areas inside municipal boundaries as 'urban'. Leads: 06B-L01, 06B-L02

findings.claim: Q1: Urban population share under a functional definition (GHSL Degree of Urbanisation: urban centres + urban clusters) applied to 2020/2025 epochs.
findings.note: Grid-based; not comparable with administrative share; report both. Leads: 06B-L08, 06B-L21

findings.claim: Q1: Urban share series from UN WUP / WDI (national definition, calendar year) for trend and to document the 2017 definitional break.
findings.note: WUP adopts national definitions; the post-2017 reclassification creates a structural break; do not interpret as migration. Leads: 06B-L05, 06B-L07

findings.claim: Q2: Household access to piped water on premises, improved sanitation (toilet type) and waste disposal method by local-level type (metro/sub-metro/municipality/rural municipality).
findings.note: Census 2021 household tables; NDHS 2022 by residence as cross-check (NDHS 'urban' uses municipal classification). Leads: 06B-L01, 06B-L02, 06B-L09, 06B-L10

findings.claim: Q2: JMP service ladders (safely managed/basic) for water and sanitation, urban vs rural.
findings.note: JMP modelled from surveys; calendar year; do not mix with census counts. Leads: 06B-L11

findings.claim: Q2: Functionality of water supply schemes and municipal solid waste collection coverage by local level.
findings.note: NWASH inventory and DWSSM reports; solid waste collection coverage requires a municipal survey (none located). Leads: 06B-L12, 06B-L13

findings.claim: Q2: Municipal capital investment need and fiscal capacity for urban services (investment plan cost vs own revenue and transfers).
Q3: Population growth 2011-2021 of secondary cities (sub-metropolitan and major municipalities outside Kathmandu Valley) on harmonised boundaries.
findings.note: Requires concordance of 2011 VDCs/municipalities to 2017 local levels; report both administrative and functional (GHSL/WorldPop) growth. Leads: 06B-L01, 06B-L04, 06B-L08, 06B-L21

findings.claim: Q3: Hazard exposure (flood/landslide class) of the fastest-growing secondary cities.
06B-A1: Growth is annualised as compound annual rate over the census interval using exact enumeration dates.
06B-A2: 'Secondary city' = sub-metropolitan cities and municipalities with a functional urban centre outside the Kathmandu Valley; list fixed after functional delineation.

data_gaps: Census 2021 household amenities tables by local level (download blocked).
Concordance of 2011 VDC/municipal units to 2017 local levels (NSO or academic; none located).
Municipal solid waste collection coverage survey (no lead).
GHSL Degree of Urbanisation applied to Nepal local-level boundaries (to compute; requires local-level boundary shapefile from Survey Department/NSO).
Municipal infrastructure investment plans and costs (DUDBC/ADB/AIIB project documents).

assumptions.text: Compound annual growth on exact census dates.
Secondary city definition as stated in findings.

challenges.text: Demographic projections that use the administrative urban share inherit the 2017 reclassification break; please carry both administrative and functional urban shares or document which is used.
Municipal service gaps must be matched to local-level fiscal capacity; please share the transfer and own-source revenue series by local-level type so 06B does not re-extract them.
Secondary-city hazard exposure uses the same ThinkHazard/BIPAD overlay; request a single shared overlay run with population by local level.

uncertainty: No values in r1. Largest uncertainty is definitional: the administrative urban share and a functional share can differ greatly for Nepal because of post-2017 municipal boundaries; growth rates depend on boundary harmonisation; service coverage differs by source type (census self-report, survey, JMP modelled, NWASH inventory). Solid waste coverage is currently unmeasurable from located sources.

definitions.definition: functional (GHSL Degree of Urbanisation; WorldPop cross-check)

urbanisation_profile.method: report both; never splice; period Census 2021 vs calendar-year international series

secondary_city_growth.method: 2011-2021 compound growth on harmonised boundaries; functional-area growth from GHSL/WorldPop; hazard flag via 13A overlay
